Subject: Potential data access incident — request for DPA notice and log coordination

Hi Lauren,

We observed unusual outbound connections from one of our test tenants (tenant-id: acme-test-42) that appear to include partial customer records. We’ve isolated a few log snippets and attached a small excerpt (acme_log_snippet.txt). At this point we don’t have full proof of exfiltration but we need to treat this as a potential personal data incident.

Per Section 6 (Incident Notification) of our DPA, can you confirm:
- Redwood’s point of contact for incident notifications and forensic cooperation;
- The expected timeline for an initial notification to Acme and for a fuller impact assessment (we note some DPAs use "without undue delay" / 72 hours);
- Whether Redwood can preserve and provide access to subprocessor logs and any corresponding custody chain.

We need an acknowledgement ASAP and an initial plan. Can you confirm within two hours?

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Head of Security
Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Potential data access incident — request for DPA notice and log coordination

Evan — thanks for the heads up and for the log snippet. Acknowledged; we’ll treat this with highest priority.

Quick answers up front:
- Point of contact: Incident response (ir@redwood.ai). I’ve looped in Rishi (security) and Marissa (customer success) to coordinate with you.
- Timeline: Redwood’s standard practice under our DPA is to notify customers "without undue delay" and to provide a more complete initial assessment within a reasonable window. To be concrete (and to give Acme a working SLA to rely on), we propose the following plan unless legal requires otherwise:
   1) Acknowledgement and initial triage within 2 hours (we’ll preserve evidence and snapshot affected nodes).
   2) Initial impact summary and scope (affected tenants/objects, suspected data categories) within 24 hours.
   3) Full technical report and remediation plan within 7 calendar days, with rolling updates as we learn more.

We prefer to avoid the ambiguous phrasing "without undue delay" in negotiations if Acme would accept an explicit 24 hour initial-impact commitment; that tends to be easier for downstream compliance teams. If Acme insists on a 72-hour regulator notification window, we can align language.

Regarding subprocessors: we use CloudWave (us-east-1) for certain logging and metrics pipelines. Rishi — can you confirm whether CloudWave-hosted logs include the traffic seen in the snippet and whether we can pull custody-preserving exports?

Please send any tenant IDs and a minimal set of example PII elements you can share. We’ll start a preserved evidence bundle immediately. I’m attaching our incident ack template and a rough timeline we’ll follow.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success (Accounts)
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Evan Brooks <security@acme-corp.com>, Marta Sanchez <marta.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential data access incident — proposed DPA redline and steps

Folks — summary and suggested legal language below. I’ve started a preservation job and opened infra ticket RWF-7191 to capture CloudWave stream exports.

Suggested redline for DPA incident clause (draft):
"Upon becoming aware of a confirmed or reasonably suspected personal data incident affecting Customer data, Redwood shall: (a) acknowledge receipt of the report and commence a triage within two (2) hours; (b) provide an initial notification to Customer outlining scope and suspected categories of personal data within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware; and (c) provide a full technical report and remediation plan within seven (7) calendar days, with rolling updates as material facts are discovered. Redwood shall reasonably cooperate with Customer’s regulators and provide custody-preserving copies of subprocessor logs where legally permissible."

Rationale: 48 hours for the initial scoped notice is more defensible operationally than 24 in complex multi-subprocessor scenarios and is tighter than generic 72-hour phrasing some customers request. If Acme legal will not accept 48, we can propose a compromise of 72 with a commitment to provide a preliminary scoped update within 24 where possible.

Operational notes:
- CloudWave is a subprocessor and we can export logs; export ETA is ~6 hours once we provide tenant and time range.
- For cross-border issues: CloudWave’s logs for the affected pipeline are stored in the US; we will provide access or redacted exports under our DPA and standard SCCs. If Acme requires additional transfer mechanisms (e.g., DPA addendum or local transfer approvals), please let us know and we’ll loop Legal.
- We should propose a short MAP today that documents: notif timeline, evidence preservation approach, who signs joint statements, and a regulator-contact plan.

I’ve attached a redline to the DPA incident section for review (redline_dpa_incident_clause.docx). If approved, I recommend we send a single consolidated email to Acme that: (1) acknowledges, (2) commits to the proposed timeline, (3) lists subprocessors and preservation ETA, and (4) proposes a short 30-min call to align.

Rishi
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Evan / Marta — thanks for the details and for working with us on this. Per Rishi’s note above, we’d like to propose the following consolidated commitments to Acme as our initial position:

1) Acknowledge + triage: Completed (this email). Evidence preservation job active (RWF-7191).
2) Initial scoped notification: We will provide an initial scope summary within forty-eight (48) hours of Redwood becoming aware; that summary will include affected tenant-id(s), suspected data categories, and preliminary mitigations.
3) Full technical report: Full report and remediation plan within seven (7) calendar days, with rolling updates.
4) Subprocessor logs: CloudWave is a named subprocessor for logging. We can export custody-preserving log exports; ETA for an export for the requested time range is approximately 6 hours from confirmation of tenant/time range. Logs will be retained according to our standard retention (90 days) and will be made available under the terms of the DPA/SCCs.
5) Cross-border transfers: Logs in scope are hosted in the US. If Acme requires additional transfer mechanisms, we will involve Legal and expedite any necessary addenda.

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm that Acme accepts 48 hours for the initial scoped notice (or indicate if you require 24 / 72).
- Share the exact time range you want exported (UTC preferred).
- Approve the attached DPA redline or provide edits, and optionally schedule a 30-min call tomorrow at 10:00am PT to finalize the MAP.

If you agree we’ll send a short formal acknowledgment and MAP with the above items and the redline attached.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
